_comment: This file is NOT a raw provider response body. No raw BatchData response body
for the Precision polygon property-search call exists anywhere in this
repository, its git history, or the local working environment.
What IS available is a set of specific, individually-cited facts that were
recorded at the time real responses were observed in production. Each entry
below records one such fact, the exact source it came from, and what it is
therefore trusted to prove. Fixtures in this directory that look like
response objects are reconstructed from these assertions and are labeled
`reconstructed_response` in manifest.json — they may not be cited as raw

assertions.fact: 3 raw strict rows and 4 broad rows were returned; every row carried intel.lastSoldDate = '2026-06-23T00:00:00.000Z' and residential R2 land use.
proves: intel.lastSoldDate exists on returned Precision polygon rows
its value is an ISO-8601 UTC datetime string at midnight, not a date-only string
the standardized land-use code on returned rows was R2
does_not_prove: the JSON path of the land-use code (recorded in prose as 'R2 land use', not as a path)
any address, coordinate, owner, valuation, or building field path

assertions.source: src/tasks/todo.md — review entry 'Fix Zero Active Properties After Confirmed-Sales Gate'
assertions.fact: A live no-write A/B preview on one polygon: with options.datasets ['basic','listing','deed','owner'] the response omitted the intel and sale objects and the job produced active=0; with dataset scoping omitted the same polygon returned active>0 with intel/sale evidence present.
proves: sending options.datasets suppresses the intel and sale objects
omitting options.datasets returns intel and sale
intel is not a member of basic|listing|deed|owner, so no datasets array can include it
does_not_prove: the per-dataset membership of any individual non-intel field

assertions.fact: BatchData rejects options.take greater than 100; paging at take<=100 succeeded.
proves: options.take has a provider-enforced maximum of 100

assertions.fact: The polygon-only control request (no date filter) returned 1 property whose intel.lastSoldDate was '2024-05-24T00:00:00.000Z'.
proves: intel.lastSoldDate is returned on the polygon endpoint with no date filter
the same ISO-8601 UTC midnight datetime format is used for older sales
does_not_prove: that a sale object was or was not present on that row

assertions.source: src/tasks/todo.md — no-write production probe on a 470.74 sq mi polygon
assertions.fact: Same polygon: no date filter returned 100 records; intel.lastSoldDate.minDate=2026-06-16 returned 10 records; minDate=2026-06-23 returned 0 records.
proves: searchCriteria.intel.lastSoldDate.minDate is honoured by the provider when combined with address.geoLocationPolygon.geoPoints
the filter narrows monotonically as minDate moves later
zero results at a 7-day window reflect provider recency lag, not a rejected request
does_not_prove: that maxDate is applied to the same returned field

assertions.source: src/tasks/todo.md — no-write provider probe on a failed polygon
assertions.fact: Rows returned at a 14-day window often carried intel.lastSoldDate plus residential land use but no listing status and no sale amount.
proves: listing status is frequently absent on Precision polygon rows
a sale amount is frequently absent on Precision polygon rows
absence of listing/sale-amount evidence is normal and must not by itself reject a row
does_not_prove: that the listing object is never present

corroborated_by: internal v15/v16 dataset research document states data?.results?.properties
unproven_paths_requiring_authorized_capt.note: Three independent internal sources agree. Still not a captured body.
extractBatchDataTotal reads all three. No evidence supports any of them. Paging currently terminates correctly on a short page, so the absence of this field is the tested behaviour.

Required for map routing. Neither coordinate shape is observed anywhere. Both aliases are retained deliberately; removing either could break production routing. This is the highest-priority item for an authorized sandbox capture.
OBS-01 proves the returned value R2 in prose. The exact JSON path is proven only on the request side (BD-E01). The response path is inferred from the request path.
